part_introductions.I. The signal and the software: A voice application becomes easier to reason about when we separate the signal from the software moving it. We begin with architectures, then inspect samples and browser media, and finally give asynchronous work explicit ownership.
part_introductions.II. Build the conversation: With formats and lifecycles established, we can connect real interfaces. A whole-file cascade exposes intermediate text; Realtime moves native audio through browser media; Gemini Live makes PCM messaging explicit. Compare their responsibilities rather than memorizing unrelated SDK recipes.
part_introductions.III. Choose and operate speech component: The model is now a replaceable part of a system we understand. We examine speech adapters and managed agents, then consider the extra responsibilities of self-hosted inference. Provider choice becomes an evidence-based deployment decision.
part_introductions.IV. Timing, trust, experience, and relea: A working audio connection is only the beginning. Natural timing, grounded tools, accessible controls, and measured operation turn it into a useful application. The final chapters connect these responsibilities into a guided production capstone.
